title: The Wise Men of Chelm and the Very Long Beam
summary: One little lane in Chelm has no synagogue, so the wise men cut a beautiful beam and try to bring it in... but the beam is long and the lane is narrow! They push, they smear on oil, they argue, and finally they decide to take the whole lane apart. Only little Gitele sees what can be done with the beam. A rhyming story based on a folk tale of the Wise Men of Chelm.
pages:
In every lane in Chelm stood a synagogue, filled with books to read,
except for one small lane, with tiny, narrow houses, indeed.
"Us too!" the neighbors called out. "We want one, it's only fair!
A synagogue of our own — please, and no arguing there!"

The wise men said, "We'll build it, we'll build it! Easy as can be!"
and climbed to the forest on the hill with an axe and a rope for the tree.
Thunk-thunk-thunk! Down fell a tree, and another, and one more,
and the beams were long — longer than ever before!

Four strong men carried a beam on their shoulders along,
and came down from the hill with their mouths full of song.
They reached the lane, and Yokel called, "Make way, here we come!"
and the neighbors peeked out of their windows, smiling, every one.

Four strong men pushed with all their might and main,
and the beam — got stuck, and wouldn't budge into the lane.
The beam is long, the alley is tight,
and oy, there's no other way in sight!

Said Reb Kalman, "We'll push even harder, we won't give in!"
So Yokel jumped on the beam and pushed... and it stayed right where it had been.
The beam is long, the alley is tight,
and oy, there's no other way in sight!

Said Reb Zalman, "We'll smear it with oil, and the beam will slide in with ease!"
They smeared it and pushed — and the beam slid back OUT, and Yokel went flying, somersaulting through the breeze.
The beam is long, the alley is tight,
and oy, there's no other way in sight!

Gitele tugged at a sleeve: "Maybe turn it — like this, on its side?"
"Shh, little girl," said Reb Shmerel. "Wise men are thinking — go stand aside!"

Reb Shmerel raised a finger and cried, "I've got it! What an idea! What a plan!
The beam is already cut — so we'll fix the lane instead, that's the way we can!"
And all the wise men clapped: "What wisdom! What a genius man!"

Carefully they took apart every wall of the lane,
and the neighbors sat outside and asked, "What's going on here? Oy, what a pain!"
Reb Shmerel smiled: "Just a moment — and there'll be plenty of room!"
And the beam lay off to the side and yawned: "This must be a dream, I assume."

But Gitele grabbed the beam by one end: "Look, you just turn it like so!"
and the beam went into the lane, the long way, straight, without a single blow.
From one end to the other it glided gracefully, with no effort at all,
and the lane stayed narrow, but the beam fit in — and nobody got squashed against a wall!

The wise men's eyes went round, their mouths fell open, and not a word was said.
Then the neighbors built the walls back up, and everyone laughed till their cheeks turned red.
And Yokel banged his hammer on the shutters: "Shabbat! A synagogue! Right here!"
And in the narrow lane stood a warm little synagogue, smelling of fresh bread — and it was ours, my dear!

The very next day they cut a new tree, long and grand to see,
and brought it to another lane, as narrow and small as a spoon could be.
The beam is long, the alley is tight —
and Gitele winked: "There IS a way in sight!"
